reasoning: Recent Georgia polling for the 2026 Senate race consistently shows Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff holding a mid–single to low–double–digit lead over Republican Rep. Mike Collins, with no credible, recent general-election presidential polling in the last 45 days specific to Georgia appearing in the gathered results. The clearest current datapoint is an August 16–17 InsiderAdvantage poll showing Ossoff +7, broadly consistent with a late-July AARP/Fabrizio-Impact poll showing Ossoff +9 and summarized coverage noting a roughly 7–9 point average Democratic edge in the race; forecaster and odds coverage describe the contest as leaning or likely Democratic, even though Georgia’s statewide Cook PVI remains slightly Republican at R+1.

sources.name: WRDW / InsiderAdvantage
sources.details: InsiderAdvantage poll of 800 likely Georgia voters finds Sen. Jon Ossoff at 50% and Rep. Mike Collins at 43% in the 2026 U.S. Senate race, a 7‑point Democratic lead.

sources.name: Breitbart (summarizing InsiderAdvantage and RCP)
sources.details: Article summarizing the same InsiderAdvantage Georgia Senate poll reports Ossoff leading Collins 50% to 43% and notes a RealClearPolling average showing Ossoff with roughly a 7.5‑point lead across recent surveys.

sources.name: AARP / Fabrizio Ward & Impact Research
sources.details: AARP/Fabrizio Ward & Impact Research poll of 1,060 likely Georgia voters shows Ossoff leading Collins 52% to 43% in the Senate race, a 9‑point advantage, while noting Collins leads among voters aged 50+.

sources.name: The Hill (on AARP Georgia poll)
sources.details: News coverage of the AARP poll reiterates that Ossoff holds a 9‑point lead over Collins, 52% to 43%, with the lead outside the poll’s ±3 point margin of error.

sources.name: Roll Call (on AARP Georgia poll)
sources.details: Coverage of the AARP Georgia survey highlights Ossoff’s 9‑point statewide lead over Collins and emphasizes his especially strong margins among voters under 50.

sources.name: Newsweek (on AARP Georgia poll)
sources.details: Article summarizing the AARP poll reports Ossoff 52% to Collins 43% and discusses demographic breakdowns of the 9‑point Democratic lead in the Georgia Senate race.

sources.name: AARP feature on Georgia 2026 poll
sources.details: AARP’s feature on its own Georgia polling notes that Ossoff leads the Senate race 52% to 43% overall, while Collins leads among voters 50 and older, underscoring a generational split within the broader Democratic edge.

sources.name: Inside Elections – Senate Report Shorts (Georgia)
sources.details: Inside Elections notes that Ossoff has maintained a healthy polling lead over Collins throughout the summer and had a 21‑to‑1 cash‑on‑hand advantage as of June 30, framing the race as currently favorable to Democrats.

sources.name: OddsShopper prediction-market analysis
sources.details: Analysis of prediction markets reports Kalshi pricing Ossoff as a roughly 91‑cent favorite versus 8–9 cents for Collins and cites a Georgia Senate model showing an average Ossoff polling lead of about 9 points and Lean/Likely Democratic ratings from most major forecasters.

sources.name: PredictionMarketsPicks – Georgia Senate 2026
sources.details: Live prediction market odds show Ossoff trading around 92¢ in the Georgia Senate market and characterize major forecasters’ ratings of the seat as Likely Democratic.

sources.name: CNN – The 9 Senate seats most likely to flip in 2026
sources.details: CNN’s ranking of the Senate seats most likely to flip moves Georgia down the list, noting Ossoff’s polling and financial advantages and implying Democrats are currently favored to hold the seat.

sources.name: Cook Political Report – Cook Partisan Voting Index (via summary table)
sources.details: Cook Partisan Voting Index table lists Georgia’s statewide PVI as R+1, indicating the state voted one point more Republican than the nation as a whole in recent presidential elections.
